description: The AFTERLIFE project publishes computational material for modelling and optimising recovery processes for food-industry wastewater. Its repository includes a Modelica process file and Python files for data, simulation and optimisation. The describing software article applies the tools to a fish-processing wastewater scenario involving membrane separation and recovery of useful fractions. GitHub exposes the source on the Replication branch, and Zenodo archives the corresponding release. The repository README explicitly assigns CC BY 4.0, making the code freely reusable despite the missing automatic GitHub licence classification. The model is not tied to one geographic region, but process inputs must be supplied for the facility being assessed. The short repository documentation leaves some dependency and execution details to the article. It supports comparison of treatment and resource-recovery configurations; no directly related catalogue record was identified.
